verdicts.title: get_training_chat_template silently changes the rendered conversation text (Jinja trim_blocks eats the newline after the wrapped expression)
verdicts.reasoning:
Reproduced end to end. transformers 5.15.1 _cached_compile_jinja_template builds ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment(trim_blocks=True, lstrip_blocks=True, ...), so a newline directly after a block tag is swallowed. _chat_template.py:326-332 (_wrap_assistant_content) splices the literal block tags _GEN_START/_GEN_END (:36-37) around the matched expression with no whitespace control, and _generation_block_marks_only_assistant (:469-520) only checks probe membership inside the generation spans - it never compares the candidate render to the untransformed render, so a text-changing transform passes. Running the real cached Hub templates through the current tree: 9 templates are accepted and 3 of them (HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta, TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, stabilityai/stablelm-2-zephyr-1_6b) render differently from the original - base '<|user|>
U1</s>
<|assistant|>
A1</s>
<|user|>...' vs transformed '...A1</s><|user|>...', i.e. the inter-turn newline after every assistant turn and the trailing newline are dropped; llama3, gemma-2, Qwen2.5, Phi-3, Mistral-v0.3 and SmolLM3 are unaffected. The assistant spans themselves stay correct (spans_ok=True). No upstream defence exists: TRL 1.10's get_training_chat_template uses hand-curated exact-match template pairs rather than a regex splice, so nothing else catches it. I downgraded severity from medium to low for one reason the finding missed: DPTrainer mutates the SAME processing_class object it later hands to super().__init__, and _dp_trainer.py:5264-5265 calls self._processing_class.save_pretrained(output_dir), so the checkpoint's tokenizer_config carries the transformed template and a consumer loading the fine-tuned checkpoint renders text identically to training. The divergence only bites when serving uses the base model's canonical template, and the magnitude is one whitespace token per turn with masking intact - real, silent, worth fixing, but not a medium-impact defect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario:
With SFTConfig(assistant_only_loss=True) on a tokenizer whose template is multi-line and not whitespace-controlled (verified on the real zephyr-7b-beta, TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 and stablelm-2-zephyr-1_6b templates - 3 of the 9 real Hub templates the transform accepts), _sft_trainer.py:426-428 overwrites processing_class.chat_template with the regex-spliced template and every row is tokenized from it. Because transformers compiles chat templates with trim_blocks=True, the newline immediately after the inserted {% endgeneration %} is deleted: training text is '...A1</s><|user|>
U2...' where the canonical template emits '...A1</s>
<|user|>
U2...', and the trailing newline is also lost. One whitespace token per assistant turn. The assistant mask is unaffected and _generation_block_marks_only_assistant never compares the two renders, so nothing warns. The fine-tuned checkpoint is self-consistent (DPTrainer saves the mutated tokenizer), so the mismatch materialises only for a consumer that renders with the base model's original template - and the saved artifact's chat_template silently differs from the upstream one it was derived from.

verdicts.title: apply_chat_template_with_mask reports a per-row truncation as a chat-template misconfiguration and aborts the whole dataset map
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with the real cached Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct tokenizer offline: get_training_chat_template succeeds, the untruncated conversation gives len(input_ids)=274 with completion_mask.sum()=12, and the same conversation with max_length=64, truncation=True raises ConfigurationError('apply_chat_template_with_mask: the tokenizer returned no assistant-token mask. This means the chat template does not carry the {% generation %} / {% endgeneration %} markers...'). Verified the code path: the template-level guard at _completion_mask.py:93-103 has already passed before :114 runs, so _has_assistant_tokens(:136-142) returning False past that point cannot mean a missing marker - it means this particular conversation rendered no assistant tokens (truncation, or a row whose last turn is a user turn). git show 62a96b72 confirms the guard changed from 'if not assistant_masks:' (true only for None/empty) to '_has_assistant_tokens', so an all-zero mask that previously passed now raises. Caller chain verified: _sft_trainer.py tokenize_row passes max_length=args.max_length and truncation=max_length is not None inside dataset.map, and SFTConfig.max_length defaults to 1024 (_sft_config.py:56), so truncation is on by default. The claim that the old path degraded gracefully also holds: _nll.py:23 and _dft.py:107/145 clamp the divisor to min=1, so an all-ignored row contributed 0.0 rather than NaN. Severity lowered from medium to low: this is fail-closed (a hard error, not silent mistraining), no privacy or numerical consequence, and the fault is the misdirected remedy plus the whole-dataset abort rather than a wrong result.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: DPTrainer with SFTConfig(assistant_only_loss=True) and the default max_length=1024 maps apply_chat_template_with_mask(..., max_length=1024, truncation=True) over the dataset. Any single conversation whose system+user prefix alone exceeds max_length (or any row that ends on a non-assistant turn) yields an all-zero assistant mask, and _completion_mask.py:114-124 raises ConfigurationError for the whole dataset.map, telling the user to install {% generation %} markers that get_training_chat_template already installed and that the guard at :93 already verified. Reproduced with Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct at max_length=64. Before 62a96b72 that row passed with an all-zero mask and contributed 0.0 loss (the NLL/DFT divisors clamp to 1), so the change turned a silently useless row into a blocking abort with the wrong diagnosis.

verdicts.title: Real gemma-3-1b-it and canonical shared-expression ChatML are still rejected, while a new test labels its parameters with those exact names
verdicts.reasoning: Both halves verified against the current tree. (a) The test ids are as quoted: test_chat_template.py:379-382 parametrizes [_LLAMA_3_TEMPLATE, _GEMMA_INLINE_TEMPLATE, _CHATML_TEMPLATE] with ids ['meta-llama-3-8b-instruct','gemma-3-1b-it','shared-chatml']. _GEMMA_INLINE_TEMPLATE (:73-80) is a synthetic one-line '{% set role = "model" if ... %}' template; the real gemma-3-1b-it template uses branch mapping, carries a multimodal content branch and a raise_exception branch, and is nothing like it. _CHATML_TEMPLATE (:40-48) has an explicit '{% elif message["role"] == "assistant" %}' branch, i.e. it is not shared-expression ChatML. Only the Llama-3 id is honest. (b) The root cause is unchanged: content_pat at _chat_template.py:450 and 'if len(content_matches) != 1: return None' at :452. Running the real google/gemma-3-1b-it chat_template through the current tree reproduces exactly what the finding claims: content_pat.finditer yields ["{{ message['content'] | trim }}", '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}'], all four wrap strategies (_wrap_assistant_content, _wrap_shared_content_expression, _wrap_gemma_shared_expression, _wrap_shared_or_clause) return None, and get_training_chat_template raises ConfigurationError('could not identify and validate an assistant-only render path'). The canonical shared-expression ChatML template is rejected the same way. OPQ-349 is not among the open tracked issues. One correction to the finding: docs/alignment/sft.md no longer names Gemma - 62a96b72 replaced 'supported shared-render templates such as Gemma and Qwen' with the generic 'selected shared-render forms' - so the docs are not themselves over-claiming; the misleading artifact is the test ids alone. Severity low: this is test-integrity/documentation, no runtime defect (the unsupported templates fail loudly with an accurate message). Note also that the fix sketch's 'exclude raise_exception from content_pat' would not be sufficient for real gemma-3, which has a second renderable content path (the iterable item['text'] loop) and emits '<end_of_turn>' outside the wrapped expression.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A maintainer reading a green test_representative_templates_render_assistant_only[gemma-3-1b-it] / [shared-chatml] concludes those two template shapes are covered. Neither is: the parameters are a synthetic inline-role-mapping template and an explicit-assistant-branch ChatML template. Running the real google/gemma-3-1b-it chat_template or canonical shared-expression ChatML through the current tree raises ConfigurationError('get_training_chat_template: could not identify and validate an assistant-only render path'), because content_pat (_chat_template.py:450) matches two expressions in gemma-3 (the content render and the raise_exception call) and the len(content_matches) != 1 bail at :452 rejects it. The runtime failure is loud and correctly worded; the defect is that the test ids claim coverage the suite does not have.

verdicts.title: language_modeling_collator(completion_only_loss=True) now silently supervises the full sequence for rows that carry no completion_mask
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced verbatim through the public facade opaque.alignment.sft.collator.language_modeling_collator on the current tree: collator(pad_token_id=0, max_length=16, completion_only_loss=True) on [{'input_ids':[1,2,3]},{'input_ids':[4,5,6]}] returns labels [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] with no completion_mask key, and on the mixed batch [{'input_ids':[1,2,3],'completion_mask':[0,1,1]},{'input_ids':[4,5,6]}] returns labels [[-100,2,3],[4,5,6]] and completion_mask [[0,1,1],[1,1,1]]. git show 08d8b1dc confirms the removed 'if self._completion_only_loss: labels_t[i,:seq_len] = _IGNORE_INDEX' branches. Two corrections that cap this at low. First, the labels half is deliberate and documented: the module design notes (_language_modeling.py:21-24) now state 'Examples without a mask retain full-sequence labels, matching TRL's language-modeling collator', and TRL 1.10's DataCollatorForLanguageModeling does take labels = example.get('labels', example['input_ids']), so the fallback does match TRL semantics - 'silently' is only true relative to the public factory docstring (:210-214), which still describes the fail-closed contract. Second, DPTrainer is guarded: _sft_trainer.py:_resolve_completion_only raises when completion_only_loss=True with neither a prompt-completion dataset nor a completion_mask, so the default trainer path does not reach this branch (the guard inspects only dataset[0], so a pre-tokenized dataset with a nullable completion_mask column could still slip through). The genuinely undocumented and indefensible part is the 'elif has_completion_mask: completion_mask_t[i,:seq_len] = 1' at :158-161, which fabricates an all-ones completion_mask for a row the caller never marked. Direct-API-only, no privacy impact, no default-path impact: low.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A caller using the exported opaque.alignment.sft.collator.language_modeling_collator directly (not via DPTrainer, which guards this at _sft_trainer.py:_resolve_completion_only) passes completion_only_loss=True and a batch in which some rows lack completion_mask. Reproduced on the current tree: the all-maskless batch returns labels equal to input_ids (full supervision, no completion_mask key), and the mixed batch returns labels [[-100,2,3],[4,5,6]] with completion_mask [[0,1,1],[1,1,1]] - the maskless row is trained on in full and its output mask is fabricated as all ones. The labels fallback is documented in the module design notes as intentional TRL-matching behaviour (though the public factory docstring still promises the opposite); the fabricated all-ones completion_mask is documented nowhere and asserts that prompt tokens are completion tokens.
